This article compares the median time to antibiotic receipt after arrival at the hospital across Danish regions and individual hospitals, a key metric for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] tracked via the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] [^src1]. Because the data is drawn from a single reporting period (2025), no historical trends can be established; however, the snapshot reveals significant disparities in how quickly patients receive antibiotics depending on where they are treated [^src1].

Nationally, the median time from hospital arrival to antibiotic administration is 272 minutes, with a wide interquartile range from 130 minutes (Q1) to 644 minutes (Q3) [^src1]. Among the five regions, Region Midtjylland performs best, with a regional median of 205 minutes, while Region Syddanmark trails with a median of 390 minutes [^src1]. 

At the hospital level, the leaders in rapid antibiotic delivery are typically smaller or regional hospitals. Bornholms Hospital is the fastest, with a median time of just 130 minutes, followed by Regionshospitalet Horsens at 154 minutes and Aarhus Universitetshospital at 171 minutes [^src1]. Conversely, the trailers are often larger university hospitals or specific regional sites. Rigshospitalet has the longest median wait time at 550 minutes, followed by Sygehus Lillebælt at 461 minutes and Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg at 428 minutes [^src1].

The data also highlights extreme outliers in the upper quartile (Q3), indicating that a significant portion of patients at certain hospitals experience severe delays. Rigshospitalet's Q3 reaches 1,521 minutes, while Sygehus Lillebælt and Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg record Q3 values of 1,615 minutes and 1,411 minutes, respectively [^src1]. These extreme spreads suggest systemic bottlenecks or specific patient complexities at these larger institutions that are not present at faster-performing hospitals like Bornholms Hospital, which maintains a tight spread with a Q3 of only 228 minutes [^src1]. The tables do not specify a formal target threshold, so compliance with a specific clinical standard cannot be evaluated from this data alone [^src1].
